logline: Seven paper cards, one per sentence of a friendly voice, explain that a content hash is a fingerprint of a render's inputs, that every output is filed under it, and that this is why a stopped render resumes where it left off.

beats.title: Hook
beats.intent: ask the question the piece answers, as the voice asks it

beats.title: Problem
beats.intent: name what went wrong before: thousands of frames and a crash that meant frame zero again; the counter runs up the frame count

beats.title: The fingerprint
beats.intent: define the hash as a fingerprint of four inputs, and show what sixty-four characters of it look like

beats.title: One folder per hash
beats.intent: show the folder named by the hash and that each frame inside carries its own hash

beats.title: Stop and resume
beats.intent: show a stopped render resuming: the frames on disk skipped, the missing one rendered

beats.title: Payoff
beats.intent: state the payoff: one frame lost, and a change that re-renders only what it touched

beats.title: Call to action
beats.intent: close on the rule in three lines and hold

substitutions.substitute: typographic diagrams: one labelled card per step on a 2.5D paper stage (the html lane), with the frame count as a counter, the hash as two rows of tabular type and the file names as captions
substitutions.reason: the html lane draws type, cards and a lit stage; it draws no arrows or icons, so each step is a card whose words and numbers are the diagram

substitutions.substitute: the narration's own sentences burnt into the frame at the bottom (assemble --job --burn-in from the SRT the voice produced), timed to the voice
substitutions.reason: the captions are then exact and in sync; the on-screen headlines say less than the voice so the two do not compete

substitutions.substitute: the local English voice af_heart, normalized to -16 LUFS
substitutions.reason: the only voice available offline; the user's own recording replaces it as a WAV

risks: the paper-flat look is near white, so the card is the look's dark slate (a stand-in, not an illustration) and the stage reads through its shadow alone; the still gate's exposure band 170 to 225 decides whether the frame is too bright

the burnt-in captions sit at the bottom of the frame in the look's body face over a paper scrim; their legibility is judged by eye on the delivery sheet, since the text-contrast check measures the shot's own text boxes
shot lengths come from the voice, so the problem and resume beats run 5.5 and 7.3 s, past the dynamic tempo's 3.5 s ceiling; cuts land on sentence boundaries, as the pacing table asks for narration
a 64-character hash does not wrap, so it is shown as two rows of 32 tabular characters
